html:
Ecuana is the name the map gives to a people of the Beni lowlands of northern Bolivia, in the seasonally flooded savanna of the Llanos de Moxos. Little is recorded about a group of this name, and it may be one of the many small peoples the Spanish and Jesuit records list in the region.

The Moxos plains were home to farming peoples who built raised fields, causeways and canals. From the late 1600s the Jesuit missions gathered many of them into mission towns. Neighbouring groups on the map include the Movima, Cayubaba and Baure.
